title: Generics Intro
concept: Generics let you write functions and types that work with ANY type, using type parameters like T as placeholders.
why: Without generics, you'd write separate functions for Int, Str, and Bool. Generics eliminate code duplication while maintaining type safety.
tips: Use square brackets [T] for type parameters — first[T] not first<T>
Name type parameters with single uppercase letters: T, U, K, V
Add constraints like T: Eq or T: Ord when your function needs to compare values
Generic code is compiled into concrete versions at compile time — no performance penalty
common_mistakes: Using angle brackets <T> instead of square brackets [T]
Forgetting type constraints — if you use == on T, you need T: Eq
Explicitly specifying type parameters when inference would work
